statement: the Ylilammi diffusion-reaction model was re-implemented to simulate how ALD growth propagates in wide microchannels, and used to map the thickness profile against process parameters and flow regimes
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: in the model the reactant partial pressure is an analytic approximation, linear then exponential along the channel
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a larger molar mass of the reactant and a larger GPC both shorten the penetration depth
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the inert gas's molecular mass and diameter matter only in transition flow, never in free molecular flow
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the slope method returns sticking coefficients systematically about 25 % above the set values; a correction factor would make it usable on Model A profiles
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the overshoot most likely comes from the analytic pressure approximation of Model A, whose pressure drops faster at the adsorption front than Model B's and steepens the half-thickness slope
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a fingerprint thickness profile needs free molecular flow, channel filling below 5 %, and the scaled profile (thickness over cycles against dimensionless distance), from which the GPC and the kinetics follow
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: to extract kinetic parameters from measured profiles the pressure must be known, since most models assume free molecular flow; different models give different parameters from the same data
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the community should share measured profiles openly as data and the models as code
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: ALD coats almost any inorganic substrate, high-aspect-ratio structures included, yet conformality there often needs tuned process parameters
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Monte Carlo methods reach beyond free molecular flow through the mean free path as a statistical parameter; every model reproduces the ideal profile, constant thickness then an abrupt fall
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the regime comparison varied one parameter at a time in free molecular and in transition flow over a single cycle, reading x̃50% and the slope from both the scaled and the Type 1 profile (Figs. S6-S15)
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: feature-scale ALD models are ballistic, Monte Carlo or diffusion-reaction; the last, on Fick's law, serve free molecular, transition and continuum flow alike through the effective diffusion coefficient
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the Thiele modulus, reaction rate over diffusion rate, tells a reaction-limited from a diffusion-limited regime; it is far above one in the latter
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: ALD kinetics are usually described by irreversible single-site Langmuir adsorption with a lumped sticking coefficient, read from the steepness of the termination profile
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the model's microchannel is wide and infinitely long, the height the limiting dimension; it describes vertical trenches as well
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the reactant enters as a step: p_A0 at the entrance during the pulse, zero otherwise; the inert gas pressure is the same inside and outside; only the reactant-A step is simulated
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Eq. (1) of Ylilammi 2018 for the collision frequency lacks Avogadro's number in both terms; Eq. (6) here corrects it
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Eq. (4) of Cremers 2019 for the collision cross section takes the sum of squared radii instead of the squared sum; Eq. (27) here corrects it
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the Langmuir step A + * ⇌ A* is a lumped, not an elementary, reaction; the real surface chemistry is more complex
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the constant free-height simplification speeds up the computation but thins each cycle's coverage somewhat too steeply in Region III; it holds while the film is thin against H and grows little beyond x50%
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Fig. 2 and Fig. S2 reproduce Figs. 2-4 of Ylilammi 2018, so the model was re-implemented correctly
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a higher reactant partial pressure and a longer pulse both lengthen the penetration depth; their product, the dose, sets it in free molecular flow, PD50% scaling as the square root of p_A t1
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: lighter reactant molecules penetrate deeper, since they diffuse faster
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a lower film density raises the thickness at constant adsorption density but leaves the penetration depth unchanged
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a higher adsorption density (GPC as areal number density) raises the saturated thickness and shortens the penetration depth, as seen experimentally
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: a high desorption probability reshapes Region II of the profile, before the fast decrease
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the sticking coefficient strongly shapes the thickness profile, as earlier diffusion-limited simulations showed
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the temperature and the inert gas pressure have only a minor effect on the penetration depth
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: besides the sticking coefficient and the dose, the reactant molar mass, the adsorption density and the film density shape the detailed thickness profile
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the film narrows the channel by twice the GPC per cycle, so the profile's shape depends on the cycle number; a fingerprint profile needs little filling (earlier under 10 %)
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Fig. 5(a),(b): a higher channel increases the penetration depth and more cycles increase the thickness, as expected
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: at constant cycles the scaled half-thickness penetration depth x̃50% first rises then falls with the channel height
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: at constant height the scaled profiles for 5 to 20 cycles about overlap; from a few percent filling the penetration depth falls with filling
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the slope at x̃50% settles to about −0.0029 for little filling in the cycle series; in the height series it rises again after a knee at Kn = 8, because wider channels move toward transition flow where gas-phase collisions lower the diffusion coefficient
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: to keep the profile independent of cycle number the filling must stay under a few percent, and the flow must be free molecular, checked by the mean free path against the limiting dimension
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Table 2: the trends differ between regimes; in transition flow a higher channel height, total pressure or reactant molar mass shortens the penetration depth and steepens the slope, and the inert gas matters
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: the scaled profile and the Type 1 normalized profile show the same trends except for q and ρ, which change the scaled slope but not the normalized one
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: at Kn ≥ 100 the effective diffusion coefficient equals the Knudsen one; the comparison used one cycle so that filling does not bias the extracted sticking coefficient
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: Model B differs from Model A in two ways: irreversible adsorption without desorption, and the pressure solved numerically from Eq. (1) instead of the analytic approximation
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: ALD processes often run in a low vacuum of roughly 1e2 Pa
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: flow regimes by Knudsen number: free molecular Kn ≫ 1, transition 0.1–10, continuum Kn ≤ 1e-3
author: 10.1039_d1cp04758b

statement: an earlier work proposed a channel filling below 10 %

statement: Model A was solved in MATLAB on an equidistant x array with the ODE23 solver (relative tolerance 1e-3, absolute 1e-5), p_A zero everywhere at t = 0, the transport properties from the previous time step

statement: each cycle: solve Eq. (21) to the pulse time, the thickness from Eq. (22), the increment and the new height from Eqs. (23)-(24), repeated to N cycles

statement: Model B (Yanguas-Gil and Elam): irreversible adsorption, p_A and θ solved together from Eq. (1) and Eq. (21) with MATLAB's pdepe in slab geometry, free molecular flow (D_eff = D_Kn), tolerances 1e-3 and 1e-6, p_A = θ = 0 at t = 0, p_A(0,t) = p_A0 and a reactive end boundary
